text:
sara: Quick sync — need decisions on audit log immutability + schema v2 + customer-facing event validation. Running into 4 open questions: RBAC delta coverage, canonical audit schema, archive retention/WORM design, and KMS key model for per-customer archives. Can we get quick feedback? :wave:

miguel: +1. For RBAC: do we log both the request and resolved permission set? e.g., when an admin changes a role, log role_before/role_after and evaluated_effective_perms?

devon: I'd prefer we store role_before/role_after + a short "evaluation_snapshot" field. Keeps diffs small but auditable. Also, we should tag events with 'sensitive=true' when permissions or secrets are touched.

ops: For storage, proposal: S3 Object Lock (GOVERNANCE mode) for primary logs + separate "archives" bucket with compliance lock (WORM) and a write-once manifest. Each archive manifest should contain fingerprints (sha256) of objects.

sara: Are we comfortable with S3 object lock + AWS KMS CMKs for encryption? How do we handle CMK rotation without breaking immutability guarantees?

devon: CMK rotation is fine — S3 stores objects encrypted with an encryption context key. But we must retain old CMKs to decrypt older archives unless we re-encrypt on rotation. Re-encrypting is heavy. Suggest per-archive CMK (customer-specific) and never rotate CMKs automatically; rotate by creating a new CMK and re-archiving. Documented process required.

miguel: Cost question: per-customer CMKs + per-tenant archive buckets could multiply keys/buckets. Can we do envelope keys + a small number of root CMKs? 

ops: Envelope encryption + a per-archive data key stored in SSM encrypted by CMK works. That lets us rotate root CMK and keep data keys valid (if you avoid key deletion). But deletion is the main risk — we must ensure KMS keys are not scheduled for deletion while archive retention in force.

sara: Validation for customer-facing audit events: customers ask for tamper-proof receipts. Two options: (1) provide signed event receipts (server signs event hash with a signing key and we expose signature+key id), (2) provide periodic signed manifests (daily) with object hashes and a signed root.

devon: Prefer option 2 for scale. We can generate daily manifests, sign with a dedicated archive signing key (HSM/KMS asymmetric), and publish an audit-receipt endpoint. Sample manifest format:

```
{
  "manifest_version": "1",
  "date": "2025-11-03",
  "archive_bucket": "redwood-audit-archives/customer-id/2025-11-03/",
  "objects": [
    {"key": "logs/2025-11-03T00:00:00-00Z/part-0001.gz", "sha256": "..."},
    ...
  ],
  "signature_kid": "kms://arn:aws:kms:...:key/...",
  "signature": "base64(...)"
}
```

miguel: Does that leak PII in manifests? We only include object keys and hashes, not event contents.

devon: Right — manifests contain only metadata (keys+hashes+counts). For customer downloads we can provide a signed bundle or SAS link.

sara: Schema changes: introducing schema v2 — we need a migration plan. Proposed fields: event_id, ts, actor, actor_type, action, resource, rbac_delta (optional), evaluation_snapshot (optional), sensitive, request_id, correlation_ids, signature_kid. Example event below:

```
{
  "event_id": "evt_01F...",
  "ts": "2025-11-03T12:34:56Z",
  "actor": "alice@example.com",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "role.update",
  "resource": "org:acme/role:billing_admin",
  "rbac_delta": {"before": ["read","write"], "after": ["read","write","manage_billing"]},
  "evaluation_snapshot": "base64(...)",
  "sensitive": true,
  "request_id": "req_123",
  "correlation_ids": ["routexxx"],
  "signature_kid": "kms://arn:..."
}
```

ops: We need to maintain both v1 and v2 for 6 months. Add an ingestion flag to denote schema_version.

miguel: What about sampling for high-volume events? We can't keep every low-signal event forever.

sara: Proposal: sampling policy table — critical events (auth, role changes, key ops) always retained for 7 years; config changes and infra-deploys retained 1 year; telemetry/log-level events sampled (1%) after 90 days. I'll draft a policy.

audit-bot: New RFC created: #A-2025-47 'audit-archive-immutability' — link: https://rfc.redwood/audit-archive-immutability :package:

devon: One more: incident response Q — if we need to revoke a key or legal-hold, we need an escalation flow. Add POA to security runbook.

sara: Action items: (1) devon: prototype manifest signer + example manifest by Fri; (2) ops: cost model for per-customer envelope keys by Mon; (3) miguel: draft RBAC coverage matrix and sampling rules by Wed. I'll sync with legal on retention minimums.

miguel: ack

devon: ack

ops: ack

sara: thanks all — leaving notes in the RFC. :thumbsup:
